newsitem.title: UK: CME denies it is buying Lithuanian TV stake.
newsitem.headline: CME denies it is buying Lithuanian TV stake.

text.p: Central European Media Enterprises Ltd on Tuesday denied a published report that it is to buy a stake in a private Lithuanian television station.
The Lithuanian newspaper Lietuvos rytas earlier on Tuesday reported that CME is to buy a 40 percent stake in private Lithuanian television station LNK.
A spokesman for CME denied to Reuters that the report was true.
The Lietuvos rytas newspaper quoted the state-owned Agricultural Bank as saying it had sold its stake in the television station to CME for an undisclosed sum.

CME, which was founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder and has its corporate headquarters based in London, holds stakes in television stations throughout Central and Eastern Europe, including Ukraine, the Czech Republic, the Slovak Republic, Romania, Slovenia, and Germany.

It will be launching operations in Poland next October with a national commercial television station and is likely to apply for national terrestrial television stations in Hungary, the CME spokesman said.
